measures.questionText: Shall Greenwood School District No. 50, South Carolina (“School District”), be empowered to issue, either at one time as a single issue or from time to time as several separate issues, general obligation bonds of the School District in the aggregate principal amount not to exceed $175,000,000, the proceeds of which shall be used for the purpose of defraying the costs of the capital improvements needed to provide modern and adequate facilities to serve the current student population and meet anticipated growth in the projected student enrollment of the School District, including the following projects: 1. Construction of new school facilities, to also include the acquisition of real property, furniture, fixtures and equipment, as follows: a. New Benjamin E. Mays Elementary School; and b. New Lakeview–Pinecrest Combined Elementary School; as well as 2. Significant renovations and additions to existing school facilities, to also include the acquisition of real property, furniture, fixtures and equipment, at the following locations: a. Eleanor S. Rice Elementary School; and b. Hodges Elementary School; as well as 3. District-wide improvement projects, including: a. Student Safety and Transportation, including the acquisition of new activity buses to safely transport students to academic, athletic, and extracurricular activities; b. Athletic and Co-Curricular Facilities, including turf field replacement and additions at high school athletic facilities and field lighting at middle and high school athletic facilities, expanding student participation in athletic and extracurricular programs; c. Modernized Classrooms, Dining Facilities and Learning Environments, including replacement of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems, upgraded classroom furniture, equipment, cafeterias, and instructional technology, playgrounds, outdoor learning environments, and updated school signage; d. Enhancements to the District’s Visual and Performing Arts programs, including the acquisition and installation of stage lighting to the Greenwood Performing Arts Center, instrument acquisition and replacement, upgrades to instrument and fine arts storage, and replacement of marching band equipment; and e. District Services Center, including the renovation of or construction of a new administrative building to consolidate district leadership, special education, student support, technology, child nutrition, and other District services currently dispersed across multiple aging school buildings into a single facility, improving access and services for students, teachers, and parents, as well as related costs, such as architectural, engineering and legal fees and costs of issuance of such bonds? CONDITIONS AND RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF TAX REVENUE COLLECTED FROM THE LOCAL OPTION SALES AND USE TAX: If approved, the total revenue collected shall be applied as a credit against the payment of any costs charged by the South Carolina Department of Revenue in connection with the collection and administration of such tax, then for the purpose of funding county and municipal operations, and against a taxpayer’s county and municipal ad valorem tax liability. measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this replacement sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Greenwood School District 50 to issue up to $175 million in general obligation bonds, at once or in separate issues, for school facilities serving current students and anticipated enrollment growth. It would build new Benjamin E. Mays Elementary and a combined Lakeview-Pinecrest Elementary, and make major renovations and additions at Eleanor S. Rice and Hodges elementary schools, including needed land, furniture, fixtures and equipment. District projects include activity buses for academic, athletic and extracurricular trips; replacement turf, additions to high school athletic facilities and field lighting at middle and high schools; heating and air conditioning, classroom furniture, equipment, cafeterias, instructional technology, playgrounds, outdoor learning areas and signs; stage lighting at Greenwood Performing Arts Center, musical instruments, fine arts and instrument storage, and marching band equipment. It also allows renovation or construction of a District Services Center to consolidate leadership, special education, student support, technology, nutrition and other district services from multiple buildings. Related architecture, engineering, legal and bond issuance costs are included.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing up to $175 million for the listed school improvements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this borrowing; the official explanation says the district could not make these improvements through this borrowing.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Chesterfield County for up to 8 years for a new county detention center costing $50 million. It also allows up to $50 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues, for the project, cost overruns and issuance costs. Covered project work includes design, engineering, land purchase where needed, construction, renovation, equipment and furnishings. Sales tax revenue would repay the bonds; if it is insufficient, taxes on all taxable property in the county would repay them.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the detention center sales tax and borrowing, including property taxes as a repayment backup.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Beaufort County until 9 years have passed or $780 million has been collected, whichever happens first, for transportation and related drainage projects. It allocates $326 million for intersections and safety, $205 million for widening, and $249 million for resurfacing and paving dirt roads. Intersection and safety work lists Ribaut Road/Lady’s Island Drive turn lanes; countywide signals; SC 170/US 278 interchange; Squire Pope Road/William Hilton Parkway; Ribaut Road in Beaufort; Lady’s Island Drive/Meridian Road; US 21 at Chowan Creek; SC 170/SC 46; SC 462 realignment; SC 170 north of the Broad; Spanish Wells Road/William Hilton Parkway; Savannah Highway/SC 170; Warsaw Island Road; Bluffton Parkway/SC 46; B.E. Wheatley Drive/Robert Smalls Parkway; US 278 at Sun City, Buck Island Road, Simmonsville Road and Old Jericho Road; Ribaut Road/Depot Road; Gumtree Road; Bluffton Parkway; Port Royal gateway on Ribaut Road; SC 46/Gibbet Road; Grober Hill Road/Parris Island Gateway; downtown Beaufort crosswalks and flashing beacons; SC 802/Short’s Landing Road; Sea Pines Circle; Evans Way/SC 170; Bluffton Parkway/Goethe Road access; US 278 median closings; Goethe Road resurfacing and traffic calming; Main Street; Grober Hill Road corridor; William Hilton Parkway’s Chaplin corridor; SC 46/Stardust Lane; Buckwalter Parkway at H.E. McCracken Circle; Joe Frazier Road/Middleton Recreation Drive; Laurel Bay/Joe Frazier and Laurel Bay/Bay Pines roundabouts; US 21 at Shanklin and Roseida roads; Woods Memorial Bridge message boards; Middle Road/SC 802 roundabout; and Middle Road guardrail between Doe and Buck roads. Widening covers Okatie Highway SC 170 and SC 46, West Fording Island Road US 278, and Robert T. Smalls Parkway/Neil Road SC 170. Dirt road paving covers Arum Circle, North Briars Creek Road, Comet Lane, Creek View Drive, Dockside Lane, Huspah Creek Drive, Judge Island Drive, Mr. McBryde Lane, Najas Drive, Nyssa Lane, O’Connor Road, Sandstone Circle, Sawgrass Court, Sparkleberry Drive, Sugar Hill Landing Road, Sweet Grass Drive, Worthington Road and Kline Circle. Resurfacing covers Beaufort, Port Royal, Hilton Head Island and Bluffton municipal roads; Daufuskie Island’s Cooper River Landing, Haig Point, Melrose Landing, Old Haig Point and Pappy’s Landing roads; US 17 and US 21 Trask Parkway; US 21 Sea Island Parkway; SC 802 Sam’s Point Road; US 21 Parris Island Gateway; SC 128 Savannah Highway; SC 170 Robert Smalls Parkway; Buckwalter Parkway; Bluffton Parkway; US 278 Fording Island Road; and US 278 Business William Hilton Parkway.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax and its listed transportation programs.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed transportation sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Beaufort County to issue up to $450 million in general obligation bonds for projects in the separate sales tax Question 1. The bonds would be repaid from the special sales and use tax in that question and must mature within 9 years.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these bonds for the Question 1 projects, with repayment from that sales tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization; the sales tax question is decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Dorchester County for up to 15 calendar years for school capital work and property tax relief. District Two receives 85% and District Four 15%. Each district would use 10% of its allocation to reduce the property tax levy for existing general obligation bond debt and 90% for its listed capital projects. District Two projects include new schools in its southern and northwestern areas near Highway 61 and Delemar Highway SC 165; academic, fine arts, outdoor athletic and career and technical work at Summerville, Fort Dorchester and Ashley Ridge high schools, with expansion at Ashley Ridge; work at Alston, Dubose and Gregg middle schools, including construction and expansion at Dubose; roofs, heating and air conditioning, equipment, furniture, special education, general education and activity buses, playgrounds, flooring, lighting, capital maintenance and technology replacement or upgrades. District Four projects include a replacement combined elementary/middle school in Ridgeville and replacement elementary school in St. George; additions and upgrades for Woodland High’s instructional programs, a fieldhouse and athletic upgrades; temporary classrooms and changes for children ages 3 to 6 at Clay Hill Elementary while its new school is built; converting Harleyville Elementary offices to classrooms and other upgrades; and converting District Office classrooms for career and technical programming.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax with the district allocations, debt-related property tax relief and listed school projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed school capital sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Charleston County for up to 6 years, starting when the current 1% school capital tax ends on December 31, 2028. Revenue would pay for the listed school capital projects and repayment of any general obligation bonds issued by Charleston County School District for them. Projects include school safety and security, controlled access, video, communications and emergency preparedness; classrooms, an annex, weight room, stadium and parking at Lucy Beckham High; a classroom wing at Johns Island Elementary; a career technology wing at Burke High; Baptist Hill Middle on the C.C. Blaney campus; replacement Meeting Street School at Brentwood; new Orange Grove Middle and PACE facilities at the former St. Andrews High campus; multipurpose rooms at Edith Frierson Montessori, East Cooper Montessori, Belle Hall Elementary and A.C. Corcoran Elementary; a Camp Road Middle car loop and James Island Elementary renovations; replacement Midland Park Primary; a new elementary school and early education classrooms for West Ashley Long Savannah growth; Baptist Hill High’s auditorium and fine arts classrooms; early education additions at Laurel Hill Primary, Drayton Hall Elementary and Hunley Park Elementary; Phase 3 work at Deer Park Middle; replacement Mary Ford Early Learning and Family Center; district athletics, including Baptist Hill’s softball field; a Pepperhill Elementary multipurpose room and classrooms; land for campus expansion, new schools or a bus lot; replacement Ladson Primary, Northwoods Middle and Montessori Community School at the former St. Andrews High campus; a new districtwide Montessori Middle and replacement Simmons-Pinckney Middle; and replacement A.C. Corcoran Elementary buildings. Capital maintenance and technology replacement, upgrades and innovation are also included.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this replacement school capital sales tax for the listed projects and related bond payments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed school capital sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Hollywood’s Town Council to issue up to $3 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues, to buy real property for the town.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this borrowing to buy real property.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Hampton County School District to issue up to $29 million in general obligation bonds, at once or over time, for projects at Hampton County High School. These include completing and equipping the athletic complex, building and equipping a greenhouse for the career and technical agriculture program, and building and equipping a separate learning center for alternative educational placements. Costs include architecture, engineering, legal work and related fees.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this borrowing for the high school projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Seneca for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and funding $31.375 million in projects. It allocates $4 million to streets, repaving, resurfacing, drainage, curbs, gutters, sidewalks and public parking lots. Another $12 million covers city cemeteries; fire station work, firefighting and emergency equipment; acquiring, designing, relocating and reconstructing the historic depot; Gignilliat Community Center; Cunningham Park; and Cherry Road water lines. The remaining $15.375 million covers downtown streets and streetscapes, Blue Ridge Park, Shaver Recreation Complex, park shelters and replacement water meters and related equipment. Projects may include renovations, replacement, conversion, equipment, furnishings and updates, with land, rights of way, demolition, utilities, parking and traffic infrastructure where needed.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and listed projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Westminster for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and funding $2,241,334 in projects. In priority order, allocations are $507,334 for Police Department renovations; $130,000 for public parking at Yousef Mefleh Memorial Fields; $95,000 for a Fire Department helicopter pad; $100,000 for depot parking resurfacing; $100,000 for Fire Department storage; $800,000 for Horton Outdoor Recreational Area parking with shade structures; and $509,000 for City Hall/Police Department public parking. The city could issue up to $2,241,334 in general obligation bonds for these projects and issuance costs while awaiting tax revenue. Sales tax revenue remaining after the required property tax credit would repay principal and interest. If it is insufficient, taxes on all taxable city property would repay the bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales tax, listed projects and bonds, including property taxes as a repayment backup.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Dillon County for up to 8 years from its start and authorizes up to $26 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues, for the listed projects. Tax revenue would repay principal and interest; if it is insufficient, the county’s full credit and taxing power would back repayment. Allocations are $1.9 million for county buildings; $375,000 for Little Rock stormwater; $2.147 million for a Latta fire station and EMS base; $650,000 each for new Hamer and Fork fire stations; $600,000 for animal shelter expansion; $13,867,731 for Dillon wastewater plant upgrades; $3,764,500 for Lake View Mill Pond RV Park; $509,500 for Lake View recreation park lighting; $136,269 for Lake View maintenance equipment; $350,000 for Latta recreation park; $300,000 for Lattimer gym’s roof; $200,000 for a Latta splash pad; and $550,000 for Latta Industrial Park water tower repairs. Eligible work includes design, construction, improvements, renovation, replacement, conversion, updates, installation, equipment and furnishings, with needed land or rights of way.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales tax and bonds for these projects, with the county’s taxing power backing repayment.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Union County for up to 15 years to pay directly or indirectly for school capital projects. The eligible facilities are Monarch Elementary, Foster Park Elementary, Buffalo Elementary, Jonesville Elementary/Middle, Sims Middle, Union County High School, Union County Career Center and Union County Achievement Academy. Work can include improvements, renovations, replacement, conversion, equipment, furnishings and updates, with land purchase, demolition, utilities, parking and traffic infrastructure where needed.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the listed school facilities and work.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed school capital sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Salem for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain town property taxes and funding $570,000 in projects. The allocations are $230,000 for Main Street repairs and revitalization, including curbs, sidewalks, drainage and the rock retaining wall; $192,000 for Town Hall modernization, repairs, renovation and additional government workspace; $63,000 for basketball and tennis court structural work, disability access and resurfacing; $62,000 to repave the town parking lot and Salem Town Park; and $23,000 for paved parking at the Police Department.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and listed projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed town sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Simpsonville for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and raising $44.4 million for road infrastructure. Projects include repaving, drainage, curbs and sidewalks throughout the city.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and road projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Mauldin for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and funding $15.6 million for roads, including repaving, drainage, curbs and sidewalks, plus $4 million for a new fire station. It also permits up to $15.6 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues, for these purposes and issuance costs. Sales tax revenue would repay principal and interest; if it is insufficient, taxes on all taxable city property would repay the bonds.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales tax, projects and bond authorization, including property taxes as a repayment backup.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Greenville for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and funding $410.145 million in projects. Allocations are $294.279 million for repaving and reconstructing roads, congestion relief, bridges, intersections, new sidewalks and sidewalk repairs; $32.374 million for stormwater and drainage; $41.912 million for critical sewer infrastructure; $17.58 million for public assembly facilities, administrative buildings and public safety; and $24 million for fire stations.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and listed projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Greenville County until 8 years have passed or $1.1 billion has been collected, whichever happens first. It allocates $990 million to highways, roads, streets, bridges, other transportation facilities and related drainage. Another $33 million would fund the county’s or jointly operated mass transit system, including operation and expansion under the Greenville Transit Authority’s Transit Development Plan, with more frequent service and expanded routes. The remaining $77 million would fund greenbelts, including buying land or conservation easements for parks, green spaces, sports fields, water access, trails and greenways; wildlife lands, floodwater management, working farms and forests; natural resource management, historic preservation, drinking water sources and water quality in rivers, lakes, wetlands and other waters, as state law permits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales tax and the listed transportation, transit and greenbelt allocations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed county sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Greenville County to issue up to $150 million in general obligation bonds for the project categories in the separate sales tax Question 1. That question’s special sales and use tax would repay the bonds, which must mature within 8 years.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these bonds for the Question 1 projects, with repayment from that sales tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization; the sales tax question is decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Travelers Rest for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes on homes occupied by their owners within city limits. It would also fund $15.826 million in projects: $3.942 million for connectors, trails and sidewalks; $2,613,500 for public parking; $4,958,500 for public assembly infrastructure; $3.062 million for critical road repairs; and $1.25 million for drainage.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the homeowner property tax credit and listed projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Marion County for up to 7 years for projects totaling $19,698,560. Allocations are $4.25 million for county law enforcement facilities and the detention center; $3.7 million for a Britton’s Neck EMS station; $2,130,650 for public works storage; $1.28 million for recreation facilities, including Gapway, St. James, Spring Branch, Sellers and Britton’s Neck parks, Centenary Community Center and Nichols Ball Field Park expansion; $920,000 for a Centenary volunteer fire A-frame metal station; $1.205 million for Marion’s C.D. Joyner Auditorium and annex; $930,000 for Eloise Grice and Watsonia recreation centers and Withlacoochee Park, including 4 pickleball courts; $850,000 for Marion’s Old Town Hall and Opera House; $150,000 for a Marion park honoring African Americans with an honoree wall; $150,000 for Marion Fire Station 15; $2.55 million for a Mullins fire station; $720,000 for a Nichols fire truck bay and storage; $460,423 for Nichols stormwater facilities; $206,487 for a new Nichols park and improvements at Tommesenia Floyd Memorial, Memorial Flag and Centennial parks; $80,000 for Nichols Town Hall; and $116,000 for Sellers Library and Resource Center. Work includes design, engineering, purchase including property where needed, construction, renovation, equipment and furnishings. The county could issue up to $20 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues, for these purposes, overruns and issuance costs. If the sales tax is insufficient to repay the bonds, taxes on all taxable county property would repay them.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales tax, listed projects and bonds, including property taxes as a repayment backup.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this sales tax and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in West Union for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain town property taxes and funding $2.05 million in projects. Allocations are $1.2 million to buy property and build or renovate the Police Department, Town Hall, Utilities Office and other government spaces; $150,000 for accessible playground equipment, other equipment and materials, picnic facilities and a dog park at Town Park; $400,000 for a splash pad, walking path, parking, driveway, state-required restroom and sewer service at 1210 West Main Street; and $300,000 for parking and pedestrian areas at the existing Town Hall.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and listed projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed town sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Spartanburg School District 2 to issue up to $156.6 million in general obligation bonds, at once or over time, to build and equip a new school for kindergarten through eighth grade in Boiling Springs and additional classrooms at Cooley Springs-Fingerville and Mayo elementary schools. Costs include architecture, engineering, legal work and related fees.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these bonds for the new school and classroom additions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Spartanburg School District 2 to issue up to $30 million in general obligation bonds only if Question 1 also passes. The bonds could be issued at once or over time for stadium upgrades at both high schools, athletic improvements at all middle schools and playground improvements at all elementary schools. Costs include architecture, engineering, legal work and related fees.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these bonds for athletic and playground improvements, conditional on approval of Question 1.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization; Question 1 is decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Walhalla for up to 8 years, providing a credit against certain city property taxes and funding projects by priority. First priority allocations are $125,000 for a fire station generator; $40,000 for fire station heating and air conditioning; $25,000 for fire station cameras and locks; $150,000 for a police station generator; $200,000 for a police vehicle entry enclosure; $220,000 for Depot Pond drainage and pipes; and $250,000 for Kaufman Square repairs and improvements. Second priority allocations are $365,000 for Sertoma parking; $350,000 for sidewalks at public facilities; $210,000 for City Hall parking and driveway; and $200,000 for a community center generator. Third priority is $600,000 for City Hall expansion.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the property tax credit and projects in the listed priorities.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed city sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Georgetown County to provide credits against county and municipal property taxes and fund county and municipal operations. Revenue would first cover the state Department of Revenue’s collection and administration costs. The official explanation says state law allows 71% of the revenue received by the county and municipalities to provide property tax credits and 29% to fund their operations.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for the described costs, property tax credits and government operations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed county sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Darlington County’s Board of Education to issue up to $250 million in general obligation bonds, in one or more issues. Projects include new Hartsville High, Spaulding Middle and Darlington Elementary schools, and upgrades at other schools and district facilities, including safety and security. If money remains, the board could prioritize other renovations, repairs, expansions, equipment and furnishings. Costs can include land, technology, construction, furniture, equipment and issuing the bonds, with project priorities set by the board over time.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this borrowing and the board’s authority to prioritize the described school projects.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Expands Aiken County’s wastewater authority previously approved in 1976 and 2006 referendums. The county could acquire, build and operate wastewater treatment facilities, provide wastewater services both inside and outside the county, and use funding from any source allowed by law.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this expanded wastewater service and funding authority.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed expansion of the county’s wastewater authority.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 0.5% sales and use tax in Charleston County until 25 years have passed or $4.25 billion has been collected, whichever happens first. It allocates $2.702 billion to roads, bridges, transportation facilities and related drainage, $858 million to operate and expand CARTA or jointly operated public transit and implement the Downtown Route Study, and $690 million to greenbelts split equally between urban and rural uses. Greenbelt uses include conservation land and easements, passive green spaces, parks, water access, natural resources, agricultural and heritage landscapes, scenic corridors and water resources. Featured road projects are Rivers Avenue’s railroad overpass at Durant Avenue; Mall Drive S-790; Patriot Boulevard widening; Better North Bridge walking and cycling work; Battery Extension West/Calhoun Street Medical District; Hagood Avenue; Maybank Highway Southern Pitchfork and roundabouts; Glenn McConnell Parkway/Magwood Road; US 17 South widening from Dobbin Road to SC 162; Johnnie Dodds Boulevard/Houston Northcutt Boulevard/Wingo Way; and Long Point Road resilience and safety. Intersection projects cover Stall Road at Midland Park and Ashley Phosphate; Ladson Road/Palmetto Commerce Parkway; Ashley Phosphate at Cross County and Brandywine; US 78/Limehouse Lane; Savannah Highway/Ashley Town Center Drive; Maybank Highway/Riverland Drive; Main Road/Mary Ann Point; SC 162/Salters Hill; SC 174/SC 164; Steed Creek Road/US 17 North; SC 45/US 17 North; and Whipple Road at Mathis Ferry and Lucy Beckham High School. Pavement work covers countywide resurfacing based on condition, traffic, safety and age, rural road safety, and roadway elevation resilience including Seabrook Island Road. Walking and cycling projects include the countywide bike/pedestrian plan, Rivers Avenue rapid transit last-mile connections, Charleston’s Safe Streets for All, Rethink Folly Road and Mount Pleasant Way plans. Other projects include 2016 tax carryovers for Dorchester Road widening and Palmetto Commerce Parkway Phase 3, coordinated traffic signals, Reynolds Avenue, a noise wall at Palmetto Commerce Interchange, and future road, bridge and drainage needs. Project design must consider bicycle, pedestrian and transit access where appropriate. If a listed project cannot be completed, its sales tax allocation goes to another listed project.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax and the listed transportation, transit and greenbelt allocations and conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed county sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Charleston County to issue up to $300 million in general obligation bonds for projects in the separate sales tax Question 1. That question’s special sales and use tax would repay the bonds, which must mature within 25 years.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these bonds for the Question 1 projects, with repayment from that sales tax.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this bond authorization; the sales tax question is decided separately.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Imposes a 1% sales and use tax in Orangeburg County to provide credits against taxpayers’ county and municipal property taxes and fund county and municipal operations.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve this sales tax for property tax credits and government operations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed county sales tax.
